lessons.title: The program we could no longer see
lessons.objective: Understand why we built Conduit before trying to define its machinery.
lessons.prose: Conduit began when one living system became too scattered to see: speech, sensors, websites, models, memory, motors, microcontrollers, and several computers.
lessons.source:
panel 0

node clock : time/ticker {
    duration_ticks = 10
    time_basis = ref("conduit.clock/monotonic-ticks")
    maximum_pending = 1
}
node drain : flow/discard

cord clock.tick -> drain.item {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 32
    max_queued_bytes = 32
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: Start the exact worker run, then inspect the admitted timer deadline and latest public text Watch.
The ticker matters because it remains alive between events instead of running once and returning.
Watch is presentation-only observation; it does not create a semantic cord.
lessons.solution: Run the checked ticker panel, witness its admitted wake and read the latest public text through the bounded Watch.

accessibility.non_audio: The complete panel, run state and latest tick are available as text; no sound or motion is required.
accessibility.keyboard: Read in document order and use Shift+Enter to start the representative panel.
accessibility.color_independent: Every runtime state is named in text and never depends on color.

lessons.title: Evictable large-value cache
lessons.objective: Cache and retrieve one bounded blob while keeping provider availability, authority, retention, integrity, and eviction outcomes explicit.
lessons.prose: Cache nodes cross an ordinary bounded host-service boundary. Put returns an opaque provider- and run-scoped handle; get verifies the content digest before yielding bytes; remove invalidates one handle. The installed provider is best effort and evictable, never durable, and a handle never substitutes for a grant.
lessons.source:
panel 0

node blob : storage/blob/literal {
    value = bytes("626f756e64656420636163686520666978747572650a")
    maximum_bytes = 64
}

node put : storage/cache/put {
    resource = secret("conduit.resource/storage-cache-example-put")
    grant = secret("conduit.grant/storage-cache-put")
    descriptor = ref("conduit.descriptor/storage-cache-example")
    run_epoch = 1
    now_tick = 10
    retention_ticks = 100
    maximum_blob_bytes = 64
    persistence = "evictable"
    eviction = "fifo"
    sensitivity = "restricted"
    cancellation = "discard"
}

node get : storage/cache/get {
    resource = secret("conduit.resource/storage-cache-example-get")
    grant = secret("conduit.grant/storage-cache-get")
    descriptor = ref("conduit.descriptor/storage-cache-example")
    run_epoch = 1
    now_tick = 11
    maximum_blob_bytes = 64
    integrity = "sha256-before-yield"
    cancellation = "discard"
}

cord blob.blob -> put.blob { capacity = 1 max_value_bytes = 64 max_queued_bytes = 64 low_watermark = 0 high_watermark = 1 pressure = block }
cord put.handle -> get.handle { capacity = 1 max_value_bytes = 66 max_queued_bytes = 66 low_watermark = 0 high_watermark = 1 pressure = block }
hints: The handle is an opaque reference scoped to this provider and run; get still needs its own active grant.
Best effort describes the provider class, while a fresh host observation describes current selectability. Neither promises future uptime.
A hit validates SHA-256 identity before bytes cross the output cord; miss, eviction, expiration, provider loss, and cancellation remain distinct outcomes.
lessons.solution: Wire an explicitly bounded blob into put, pass only its opaque handle to get or remove, pin a fresh provider report and separate operation grants in the exact plan, and request evictable retention only.

accessibility.non_audio: An ordered text table names provider observation freshness, best-effort class, resource and grant, blob digest and byte count, opaque handle scope, queue pressure, retention, hit or miss, cancellation, error, and terminal cause.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the ordered cache story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Every state is duplicated by provider, handle, digest, bound, hit, miss, evicted, expired, cancelled, error, and terminal text.

library.summary: Explicit typed cache nodes store bounded blobs through an optional best-effort provider without claiming durability.
library.what: Blob literal produces bounded bytes; put stores them and returns an opaque handle; get checks identity before a hit; remove invalidates the referenced entry.
library.when: Use this profile when recomputable large values may be retained locally for reuse and a miss or provider loss can be handled explicitly.
library.wrong: Durable requirements, stale reports, insufficient capacity, oversized values, denied grants, refused sensitivity, digest mismatch, wrong provider or run handles, cancellation, eviction, expiration, and provider loss fail or report explicit outcomes with no hidden fallback.
library.provider: explicit browser in-memory evictable cache provider through the ordinary exact host-service boundary
expected_evidence: known contract, installed provider, fresh host observation, best-effort availability class, active operation grant, and resource binding
exact implementation, artifact, descriptor, provider epoch, run epoch, handle slot and generation, content digest and byte count
finite entry, byte, retention, pending-operation, queue, timer, cancellation, and evidence bounds
ordered put then integrity-checked hit, or explicit miss, eviction, expiration, remove, provider loss, cancellation, error, and terminal cause
protected resource and grant configuration remains redacted

lessons.title: A live ticker Watch
lessons.objective: Run one continuous ticker in the production executor and observe its latest public text through a bounded Patchbay Watch.
lessons.prose: Start owns one exact worker session. Active means a bounded pump is doing admitted work; Waiting means this same epoch owns a named timer or host interest and is not finished. Quiesce stops new admissions, Drain preserves accepted work, Abort returns queued work, and Terminal is final. The ticker emits public text, the discard node consumes it without retaining value history, and Patchbay copies only the latest admitted preview. Watch is isolated runtime instrumentation: removing it leaves this same panel, plan, demand, timing, and cord pressure running. Adding a semantic tee would edit this panel and exact plan; adding a lossless recorder would be a plan-visible node or evidence stream and could apply its declared pressure. Freeze Display pauses only Patchbay advancement: the production executor, timer wakes, bounded evidence cursor, and Watch cursor continue, then the display resumes at the latest bounded state. Separately, the worker commits ordered run evidence into the exact plan's finite evidence-byte budget before scheduler slots are reused. That rolling history has monotonic cursors: a reconnect resumes at its saved cursor, or receives an explicit gap and the earliest cursor still available. Protected material remains structurally visible but redacted. Unsupported renderers and abrupt browser placement loss remain textual facts rather than invented execution states. Strict audit instead stops when required evidence cannot be committed. The browser schedules explicit timer wakes; it does not execute the graph or own the evidence store.
lessons.source:
panel 0

node clock : time/ticker {
    duration_ticks = 10
    time_basis = ref("conduit.clock/monotonic-ticks")
    maximum_pending = 1
}
node drain : flow/discard

cord clock.tick -> drain.item {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 32
    max_queued_bytes = 32
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The time/ticker provider remains Waiting between exact timer deadlines.
The Watch is latest-only, public, bounded, and cannot backpressure the cord.
The evidence accounting names its earliest and next cursors. After an observer pause, resume there or accept the explicit gap; never invent evicted rows.
Rolling service history may evict committed rows, while strict audit fails closed instead of losing required evidence.
Stop aborts this same epoch; source edits never recreate it.
lessons.solution: Connect time/ticker to the bounded discard sink, Start once, attach the plan-admitted text Watch, and keep advancing only the exact pending deadline until Stop.

accessibility.non_audio: The latest tick, run state, exact timer deadline, plan identity, resident value accounting, evidence bounds, earliest cursor, next cursor, and dropped-row count remain visible as live text; no sound or motion is required.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Shift+Enter to Start, W to attach or remove the admitted Watch, F to freeze or resume presentation outside the editor, and ArrowRight to inspect the ordered ticker event table while it has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Active, Waiting, wake, tick, cleanup, and terminal states are written in the ordered table and never depend on color or animation.

library.summary: One exact ticker session alternates between bounded Active work and Waiting on its admitted timer while Patchbay observes only the latest public text.
library.what: The ticker publishes one public text value, becomes Waiting on one exact timer interest, and resumes the same run and epoch after the host delivers that named wake.
library.when: Use the ticker when a graph needs an open-ended, plan-bounded monotonic tick stream whose host clock behavior remains explicit.
library.wrong: Completing after one tick, starting a new run per tick, immediately jumping real hosted time, retaining Watch history, or treating presentation polling as execution all violate the current contract.
library.provider: the exact hosted provider adapter with deterministic browser timer wakes and a separately mapped real hosted clock
expected_evidence: one Start with one fixed plan, run, epoch, provider, clock, timer, queue, Watch, and evidence admission
Active publication followed by Waiting on the exact next timer deadline
a named host wake resuming the same epoch without an immediate real-clock jump
Abort, bounded cleanup, and one terminal result for the already active session

lessons.title: A small isolated network without robot authority
lessons.objective: Build a small standing network in explicit stages: begin with two isolated application endpoints, add link and address readiness, DHCP and a local name, then a route, listener, bounded exchanges, observation, failure, recovery, Waiting, and explicit stop.
lessons.prose: This is a standing semantic network graph, not an imperative setup script. The project begins with two isolated application endpoints and adds one semantic layer at a time: a time-bounded link and address observation, finite DHCP, an expiring local name, an authored route, a repeated-session listener, packet/datagram/stream exchanges, and explicit observation. Each executable stage remains present while providers wait; the assembled topology is also checkable as one bounded design. Link, frame, packet, datagram, byte stream, session, control event and retained state stay visibly different. Loss, expiry, provider loss and cancellation are outcomes to observe and recover from, not reasons to invent topology. No route installation, bridge, forwarding, NAT, firewall, Internet, membership or robot authority is inferred from a cord. A physical Linux or Pico binding must separately supply its exact provider observation, resource, grant and use-time lease.
hints: Describe-only inventory has no provider observation and cannot start the fixture or a radio.
The ninth DHCP client, stale registration, wrong boot/device, ICMP overflow, port or mDNS conflict, cancellation, reboot and provider loss each have distinct bounded outcomes.
No network value can become a Create UART handle, possession lease, safety grant or motor authority.
lessons.solution: Keep every requested network limit in the exact plan, bind physical execution only through fresh host evidence and an enforced effect backend, and retain explicit ownership boundaries for transports, application sessions, discovery and robot authority.

accessibility.color_independent: Every state is duplicated by an exact identity, numeric bound, ownership label, diagnostic or terminal word.

lessons.objective: Keep the readable authored program separate from the exact plan, the currently active run, and the evidence that run leaves behind.
lessons.prose: The capsule carries the exact Panel source, its named revision, lock facts, explicit artifact identities, and optional layout. Checking it offline proves that the authored document is well formed; it does not prove that this machine has a provider or authority. Resolve creates a separate exact plan. Starting that plan creates a live epoch. Execution appends bounded evidence. Editing source or moving a box never rewrites an already admitted plan, live epoch, or evidence record.
